unmapped_findings: Charpy impact characteristic loads at RT (from Fig. 9c,d load-deflection analysis): general yield load Fgy ≈ 17 kN, maximum load Fm ≈ 24.5 kN, crack initiation load Fin ≈ 22.5 kN, load ratio Fiu/Fm ≈ 0.83, and rebound compliance RC = 3.7864 (no dedicated field for these instrumented impact values).
Charpy impact total absorbed energy W_all at RT is about 327 J, the highest of the three test temperatures (277 J at −77 °C and 188 J at −196 °C), indicating the best overall impact toughness at RT.

Crack initiation energy W_initiation of the RT impact sample is 57 J (vs 68 J at −77 °C and 112 J at −196 °C); the lower W_initiation at RT acts together with higher crack-propagation energy to give the maximum W_all.

RT impact fracture surface characteristics: shear lips present, the largest fibrous zone, the smallest (most compressed) fracture surface area and the most obvious ductile fracture features, with the largest and most equiaxed dimples in the radial zone (Fig. 6c,f), indicating better toughness at higher temperature.

Secondary cracks are present near the fracture after the RT impact test (unlike at −196 °C); they release stress concentration at the primary crack tip and redistribute stress, delaying fracture and giving a higher crack-propagation energy at RT.

Near-fracture SEM of the RT impact sample shows the most abundant and most pronounced planar-glide slip-band traces (six arrowed features in Fig. 11c) among the three test temperatures; only few regions experienced planar glide at −196 °C.
The RT impact sample exhibits higher crack-propagation energy but lower crack-initiation energy relative to the cryogenic samples; the primary crack path is zigzag and predominantly transgranular.
